newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says shipped more than 80,000 T grain via U.S.
newsitem.headline: CWB says shipped more than 80,000 T grain via U.S.

text.p: More than 80,000 tonnes of Canadian Wheat Board grains were shipped through the United States since early January, a CWB official said.

"If you add it all up, it's a little over 80,000 tonnes we've moved through the U.S. to Portland or the Gulf last I checked about a week ago, so there may be a little more to add to that," CWB spokesman Brian Stacey said.
All the grain was shipped in Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp hopper cars and locomotives, Stacey said.

Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure led to delays in rail shipments to Canada's Pacific ports since early January, forcing the shipments through U.S. ports. The Canadian Wheat Board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines and has deferred some sales.
There were seven vessels loading Canadian grain at Pacific port Tuesday and 33 were waiting, one as long as 46 days, Stacey said.
